subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit & streaming UX notes (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery notes & next steps — Acme Health streaming pilot

Thanks again for the demo today — we appreciated the walkthrough. A quick recap from our side and a few open questions so we can prioritize the pilot: 

- Problem: our provider chat UI frequently shows partial/garbled lines when responses stream in, and users sometimes see mid-sentence truncation or repeated tokens.
- Constraints: target p95 end-to-end latency of 800ms for short queries (<40 tokens) and <2s for longer/streaming responses.
- Priority: coherence of partial output (no mid-phrase hallucinations), reliable stop sequences to avoid trailing system tokens, and consistent quality across sessions (we cannot tolerate regressions after model swaps).

Could you share recommended model variants, any benchmark links or sample prompt sets you'd like us to run, and an initial plan to validate streaming UX (metrics + test harness)? If there's a mutual action plan we can follow, that would help us get legal/procurement moving.

Also looping in Priya (PM) who owns the UI experience; Priya, happy to add other stakeholders.

Thanks,
Alex Nguyen
Product Lead, Conversational AI
Acme Health

Attachments: none (will need your prompt set + benchmark links)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery notes & next steps — Acme Health streaming pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear summary, and great to meet you and Priya yesterday. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Goal: ship a streaming experience that avoids partial/coherent breakage, enforces deterministic stop sequences, and stays within your latency SLOs.
- Risks you called out: partial output coherence, stop-sequence mishandling, and regressions after model changes.

Recommended next steps (proposed timeline):
1) Technical eval (3-5 business days): Jordan will run a model-fit eval across 3 candidate variants and your prompt set (attached). He'll produce a benchmark with per-token latency, prefix-coherence metric, stop-sequence failure rate, and quality regressions vs your golden prompts.
2) Streaming UX test (2 business days): run a small canary (1000 sessions) using our streaming endpoint with KV-prefetch enabled + prefix caching to measure real-world p50/p95 latency and truncation incidents.
3) Canary rollout & policy: if metrics look good, we do a 2-week canary with automatic fallback to a lower-latency variant.

What I'll attach: prompt_sets_v2, our model_recommendations doc, and an example benchmark template. Jordan — can you run the eval by EOD tomorrow and upload the CSV to the shared link?

Deliverables / asks for Acme:
- Confirm the prompt set matches your production prompts (Priya)
- Provide a list of 3-5 representative long-form dialogs (for regression checks)
- Approve the canary window and the fallback policy

I'm attaching the prompt set + model recommendations now. Happy to hop on a 30m call to align on the canary schedule if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_streaming_prompt_sets_v2.pdf, model_recommendations.md

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery notes & next steps — Acme Health streaming pilot

Thanks — I started the eval across the 3 variants Marissa recommended (gpt-stream-13b-v1-std, gpt-stream-7b-q4f, and gpt-stream-13b-v1-quant). Initial plan and notes: 

Eval plan:
- Dataset: acme_streaming_prompt_sets_v2.pdf (thanks Marissa) + the 5 long-form dialogs you mentioned (please share).
- Metrics: per-token processing latency, network-to-client streaming latency, prefix-coherence (we compute a partial-output BLEU-ish coherence score on prefixes), stop-sequence failure rate, and quality delta vs your golden responses (ROUGE/embedding-sim).
- Harness: we'll run synth load and real-request replays from a region close to your users (us-west) to capture realistic latency. Results will be in a CSV and uploaded to the S3 link below.

Initial findings (preliminary, sampling 200 sessions):
- gpt-stream-13b-v1-std: best coherence, stop-sequence success 99.6%, median server-side token latency ~15ms, median end-to-end p95 estimate ~740ms for short queries.
- gpt-stream-7b-q4f: good latency (p95 ~520ms) but we saw slight prefix incoherence on certain multi-turn prompts (repetition on turn boundaries).
- gpt-stream-13b-v1-quant: promising cost/latency tradeoff but stop-sequence failures higher (~1.8%); likely due to how decoding interacts with quantized logits in our current runtime path.

Notes on the partial-output truncation: most truncation cases we've seen in other customers are due to client-side stop handling (e.g., UI closes SSE stream on seeing a substring match) or aggressive server-side max_tokens enforcement when using streaming + chunked KV cache. For Acme, I recommend:
- Server-side: use our recommended stop sequence pattern (###END_RESPONSE###) and enforce final-token flush.
- Client-side: ensure the UI doesn't treat interim punctuation as a final stop; ideally inspect the full stop token boundary.

Next steps (technical):
- I'll upload the full benchmark CSV to s3://redwood-benchmarks/acme/2026-10-19/latency-report.csv by EOD.
- Propose running the 1000-session canary tomorrow morning local to us-west; will include auto-fallback to gpt-stream-7b-q4f if p95>900ms or stop-failure>0.5%.

Let me know your availability for a quick sync today — I can walk through the CSV and the specific failing prompt examples.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: benchmark_latency_report_20261019.csv
Links: s3://redwood-benchmarks/acme/2026-10-19/latency-report.csv

From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery notes & next steps — Acme Health streaming pilot

Thanks Marissa & Jordan — this is helpful and aligned with what we need. A few clarifying Qs before we kick the canary: 

1) For the stop sequence recommendation (###END_RESPONSE###) — will that add visible tokens to the user experience if the client forgets to strip them? In other words, do we need the client to explicitly strip the stop marker, or can your streaming endpoint guarantee it's not emitted to the UI?
2) For the fallback policy: can you confirm the expected p95 budget under both gpt-stream-13b-v1-std and gpt-stream-7b-q4f for our typical short queries (we measured avg token length 18)? Those numbers will help our infra team approve the canary.
3) For regressions: can your eval include a delta-flagging step where we alert if embedding-sim drops >0.02 vs golden? We want automated gating.

Priya and I can be on a 30m call today at 11:00 PT to align on the canary and action items. If you can send the S3 link and the CSV, we'll review prior to the call.

-Appreciate the fast turnaround — Alex

Alex Nguyen
Product Lead, Conversational AI
Acme Health
